answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by tying voting power to capital locks. If an attacker attempts to flood the network, the economic cost of acquiring a majority stake reaches a nadir when liquidity is thin. A sudden gale of malicious nodes will trigger an immediate pulse of slashings, burning the attacker's collateral. By binding identity to assets, the mechanism ensures that faking nodes requires prohibitive financial expenditure, rendering large-scale deception irrational and unsustainable.
